preserved_contract_exceptions.name: Explicit remote loopback gateway
preserved_contract_exceptions.description: A Moonshot/OpenRouter role explicitly configured to 127.0.0.1, localhost or ::1 may use HTTP/HTTPS with a valid port and receive the selected provider Bearer credential. This deliberate gateway route is not the public-provider HTTPS path, and is separately exercised in the review. Local backend roles still forbid Authorization.

dependency_evidence.observation: Context7 confirms AsyncClient does not follow redirects by default, while trust_env defaults true; the patch fixes both flags explicitly and MockTransport checks the behavior.
trust_env=False disables environment-derived proxy and certificate configuration; no actual environment proxy or provider connection was used.

limitations: The source, tests and independent harness ran only with wholly synthetic environment/credentials, dotenv blocked before imports, MockTransport/registrars and denied socket/DNS operations. No provider, real key, native service, hardware, operator telemetry capture or ATTESTED object was used.
Checks establish application routing and SDK behavior in memory; they do not certify real DNS resolution, TLS negotiation/certificate chain, network isolation or endpoint service behavior.

The loopback allowance is a hostname/address contract. Actual host resolution and an explicitly configured local gateway remain trusted deployment inputs; no claim that all remote-backend requests are HTTPS is made.
The frozen snapshot covers backend, URL, credential, model and timeout. General cross-thread mutation safety and deep immutability of caller-owned message objects are not claimed.

Removing implicit load_dotenv is intentional: callers must supply configuration explicitly or through their established process environment. api_key remains available for the inspected cognitive_pilot consumer.
Secret checks cover module error results/logs and exposed config repr, not arbitrary external logging/tracing configured by other code.
